_readme: LISTENING TESTS
PLAYBACK. Each test is spoken by the browser's own speech engine unless it
has an "audio" field, in which case that recording is played instead:
"audio": "downloads/listening/l07-1.mp3"
Adding that one field switches a test from browser speech to a recording.
Nothing else in the test changes, so MP3s can replace speech one test at a
time whenever recordings become available.
MODES. Every test offers Practice (replay freely) and Formal test (the
recording plays twice only). The student chooses; the default is Practice.
Fields for each test:
id           used by <div data-listening="ID"> on a page
grade        6 to 11
rate         base speaking rate. Lower is slower and clearer. The
speed control multiplies this, so a Grade 6 passage stays
slower than a Grade 11 one at every setting.
instructions what the student is told to do
script[]     speaker + text. Distinct speakers get distinct voices where
the device offers more than one English voice.
questions[]  see the six kinds below
Question kinds:
mcq        prompt, options[], answer (position from 0), explanation
gap        prompt, answer (word or list of acceptable words), explanation
short      prompt, answer (or list), explanation
note       prompt, lines[] each with label and answer, explanation
match      prompt, pairs[] with term and meaning, explanation
sequence   prompt, items[] IN THE CORRECT ORDER, explanation
The transcript is built from script[] and is written into the page only
after the student submits. After editing this file, run build.cmd.

tests.title: At the school office
tests.description: A short conversation between a student and the school clerk. Competency levels 1.1 and 1.2 (2026 syllabus): listens to a simple functional text and extracts the information conveyed.
tests.instructions: Listen to the conversation and answer the questions. Submit to see your score, the answers and the transcript.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Listen to a conversation at the school office.

script.speaker: Clerk
script.text: Good morning. How can I help you?

script.speaker: Dilini
script.text: Good morning, madam. I have come to collect a form for the sports meet.

script.speaker: Clerk
script.text: Certainly. What is your name and your class?

script.speaker: Dilini
script.text: My name is Dilini Perera. I am in Grade six B.

script.speaker: Clerk
script.text: Here is the form. Please bring it back before Friday, signed by your parent.

script.speaker: Dilini
script.text: Thank you very much, madam. Should I bring anything else?

script.speaker: Clerk
script.text: Yes. Bring one photograph as well. A small one is enough.

script.speaker: Dilini
script.text: I will bring both on Thursday. Thank you.

questions.prompt: Why has Dilini come to the office?
options: To collect a form for the sports meet
questions.explanation: She says she has come to collect a form for the sports meet.

questions.prompt: Complete: Dilini is in Grade six ____.
questions.explanation: She says she is in Grade six B.

questions.prompt: By when must the form be returned?
questions.explanation: The clerk says to bring it back before Friday.

questions.prompt: What must a parent do to the form?
questions.explanation: The clerk says the form must be signed by a parent.

questions.prompt: Complete the notes about what Dilini must bring.
questions.explanation: She must bring the signed form and one small photograph.

questions.prompt: On which day does Dilini say she will bring both things?
questions.explanation: She says, 'I will bring both on Thursday.'

tests.title: A school announcement
tests.description: An announcement made over the school public address system. Competency levels 1.1 and 1.2 (2026 syllabus): listens to a simple functional text and uses its information.
tests.instructions: Listen to the announcement. Complete the notes and answer the questions, then submit.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Listen to an announcement at a school.

script.speaker: Teacher
script.text: Good afternoon, students. Please listen carefully. The inter-house athletics meet will be held on the twenty second of September.

script.speaker: Teacher
script.text: It will begin at eight o'clock in the morning at the main playground.

script.speaker: Teacher
script.text: All students must wear their house colours and bring a water bottle and a cap.

script.speaker: Teacher
script.text: Students who wish to take part in the long jump should give their names to Mr Silva before Wednesday.

script.speaker: Teacher
script.text: Parents are welcome. Thank you.

questions.prompt: Complete the notes about the athletics meet.
questions.explanation: The announcement gives the date as the twenty second of September, the time as eight o'clock in the morning, and the place as the main playground.

questions.prompt: What must all students wear?
questions.explanation: The teacher says all students must wear their house colours.

questions.prompt: Match each item to the reason it is mentioned.

pairs.meaning: The teacher who takes names for the long jump
The day by which names must be given

questions.explanation: Students must bring a water bottle and a cap; names for the long jump go to Mr Silva before Wednesday.

questions.prompt: Who is welcome to attend?
questions.explanation: The announcement ends by saying parents are welcome.

questions.prompt: Apart from a water bottle, what else must students bring?
questions.explanation: The teacher says to bring a water bottle and a cap.

questions.prompt: Which event needs students to give their names in advance?
questions.explanation: Only the long jump is mentioned as needing names in advance.

tests.title: Meet my family
tests.description: A student describes the people in her family. Competency levels 1.3 and 1.4 (2026 syllabus): listens to a simple informational text and uses the information conveyed.
tests.instructions: Listen to Sanduni describing her family, then answer the questions and submit.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Listen to a student talking about her family.

script.speaker: Sanduni
script.text: Hello. My name is Sanduni and I live in Kurunegala. There are five people in my family.

script.speaker: Sanduni
script.text: My father is a farmer. He grows vegetables and he leaves the house very early every morning.

script.speaker: Sanduni
script.text: My mother is a teacher at a primary school. She teaches small children and she loves singing.

script.speaker: Sanduni
script.text: My elder brother, Kasun, is seventeen. He plays cricket for his school team.

script.speaker: Sanduni
script.text: My little sister, Ruwani, is only four years old. She is always asking questions.

script.speaker: Sanduni
script.text: We also have a dog called Kalu. He sleeps under the mango tree all day.

questions.prompt: How many people are there in Sanduni's family?
questions.explanation: She says there are five people in her family. Kalu is a dog, not a person.

questions.prompt: Match each person to what is said about them.
questions.explanation: Each family member is given one clear detail in the passage.

questions.prompt: Complete: Sanduni lives in ____.
questions.explanation: She says she lives in Kurunegala.

questions.prompt: How old is Ruwani?
questions.explanation: Sanduni says her little sister is only four years old.

questions.prompt: Where does the dog sleep?
questions.explanation: She says Kalu sleeps under the mango tree all day.

questions.prompt: What does Sanduni's mother love doing?
questions.explanation: The passage says her mother loves singing.

tests.title: Getting ready for a trip
tests.description: A mother and son plan what to pack. Competency levels 1.1 and 1.2 (2026 syllabus): listens to a simple functional text and uses its information creatively.
tests.instructions: Listen to the conversation. Put the events in order, complete the notes, then submit.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Listen to a mother and her son getting ready for a trip.

script.speaker: Mother
script.text: Nuwan, we are leaving for Anuradhapura tomorrow. Have you packed your bag?

script.speaker: Nuwan
script.text: Not yet, amma. What should I take?

script.speaker: Mother
script.text: First, put in two shirts and two pairs of trousers. Then add your toothbrush and a towel.

script.speaker: Nuwan
script.text: Can I take my camera?

script.speaker: Mother
script.text: Yes, but pack it last, at the top, so that it does not get crushed.

script.speaker: Nuwan
script.text: What time will we leave?

script.speaker: Mother
script.text: The bus goes at six in the morning, so we must wake up at half past four.

script.speaker: Nuwan
script.text: That is very early. I will go to bed straight after dinner.

questions.prompt: Put the packing steps in the order the mother gives them.
questions.explanation: She says to put in clothes first, then the toothbrush and towel, and to pack the camera last.

questions.prompt: Complete the notes about the journey.
questions.explanation: They are going to Anuradhapura; the bus leaves at six and they must wake at half past four.

questions.prompt: Why must the camera be packed at the top?
options: So it is easy to find
So it does not get crushed
questions.explanation: The mother says to pack it last, at the top, so that it does not get crushed.

questions.prompt: Complete: Nuwan must pack two shirts and two pairs of ____.
questions.explanation: The mother says two shirts and two pairs of trousers.

questions.prompt: What does Nuwan say he will do straight after dinner?
questions.explanation: He says he will go to bed straight after dinner because they must wake up early.

questions.prompt: Has Nuwan packed his bag when the conversation begins?
questions.explanation: He answers, 'Not yet, amma.'

tests.title: The lost kitten
tests.description: A short story read aloud. Competency levels 1.5 and 1.6 (2026 syllabus): listens to a simple literary text and uses its information creatively.
tests.instructions: Listen to the story, then answer the questions and submit to see your score and the transcript.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Listen to a short story.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: One rainy evening, Tharu heard a small sound near the gate. It was thin and high, like a whistle.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: She took an umbrella and went out. Under the hedge, wet and shivering, sat a tiny grey kitten.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Tharu carried it inside and dried it with an old cloth. Her mother warmed a little milk.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: The kitten drank everything and then fell asleep in Tharu's lap.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: The next morning, a neighbour knocked at the door. She was looking for her kitten, which had run away in the storm.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Tharu was sad to give it back. But the neighbour smiled and said, 'You may visit her whenever you like.'

questions.prompt: What was the weather like when Tharu heard the sound?
questions.explanation: The story begins on a rainy evening.

questions.prompt: Put the events in the order they happen in the story.
items: Tharu hears a sound near the gate
She finds a kitten under the hedge
A neighbour knocks at the door
questions.explanation: The story moves from hearing the sound, to finding the kitten, to the milk, and then to the next morning.

questions.prompt: What colour was the kitten?
questions.explanation: The story says it was a tiny grey kitten.

questions.prompt: How did Tharu feel when she had to give the kitten back?
questions.explanation: The story says Tharu was sad to give it back.

questions.prompt: Why had the kitten run away?
options: It was frightened by the storm
questions.explanation: The neighbour says her kitten had run away in the storm.

questions.prompt: Complete: The neighbour said Tharu may ____ the kitten whenever she likes.
questions.explanation: The neighbour smiles and says, 'You may visit her whenever you like.'

tests.title: Directions to the post office
tests.description: One person asks another the way. Competency level 3.2: listens and follows instructions and responds to requests.
tests.instructions: Listen to the directions and follow them carefully. Answer the questions, then submit.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Listen to a visitor asking for directions.

script.speaker: Visitor
script.text: Excuse me. Could you tell me the way to the post office, please?

script.speaker: Local
script.text: Certainly. Walk straight down this road until you come to the traffic lights.

script.speaker: Local
script.text: At the lights, turn left. You will pass a bakery on your right.

script.speaker: Local
script.text: Keep walking until you see a large temple. The post office is just opposite the temple.

script.speaker: Visitor
script.text: Thank you. Is it far?

script.speaker: Local
script.text: About ten minutes on foot. It closes at four, so you have plenty of time.

script.speaker: Visitor
script.text: That is very kind of you. Thank you.

questions.prompt: Put the directions in the correct order.
items: Walk straight to the traffic lights
Pass the bakery on your right
questions.explanation: The directions are given in this order: straight to the lights, left, past the bakery, then the temple.

questions.prompt: Which way must the visitor turn at the traffic lights?
questions.explanation: The local says, 'At the lights, turn left.'

questions.prompt: Where exactly is the post office?
questions.explanation: The post office is just opposite the temple.

questions.prompt: Complete: The walk takes about ____ minutes.
questions.explanation: The local says it is about ten minutes on foot.

questions.prompt: At what time does the post office close?
questions.explanation: The local says it closes at four.

questions.prompt: On which side of the road is the bakery?
questions.explanation: After turning left, the visitor will pass a bakery on her right.

tests.title: An announcement at the railway station
tests.description: A public announcement about train times and platforms. Competency level 3.1: responds to simple announcements.
tests.instructions: Listen to the announcement and complete the notes. Then answer the questions and submit.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Listen to an announcement at a railway station.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Attention, please. The intercity train to Badulla will depart from platform three at ten forty five.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: This train is running twenty minutes late. We are sorry for the delay.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Passengers travelling to Kandy should go to platform one. That train leaves on time at eleven o'clock.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Please do not leave your luggage unattended at any time.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Thank you for travelling with us.

questions.prompt: Complete the notes about the two trains.
questions.explanation: The Badulla train leaves platform three at ten forty five; the Kandy train leaves from platform one.

questions.prompt: How late is the Badulla train?
questions.explanation: The announcer says the train is running twenty minutes late.

questions.prompt: Which train is running on time?
questions.explanation: The Kandy train leaves on time at eleven o'clock.

questions.prompt: At what time does the Kandy train leave?
questions.explanation: The announcement says it leaves at eleven o'clock.

questions.prompt: What are passengers warned not to do?
questions.explanation: The announcer says not to leave luggage unattended at any time.

questions.prompt: Complete: The train to Badulla is an ____ train.
questions.explanation: The announcement calls it the intercity train to Badulla.

tests.title: How to make a paper bookmark
tests.description: A teacher explains a craft activity step by step. Competency level 3.2: listens and follows instructions.
tests.instructions: Listen to the instructions carefully. Put the steps in order and answer the questions, then submit.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Listen to a teacher explaining how to make a bookmark.

script.speaker: Teacher
script.text: Today we are going to make a paper bookmark. You will need card, scissors, glue and coloured pencils.

script.speaker: Teacher
script.text: First, cut a strip of card about twenty centimetres long and five centimetres wide.

script.speaker: Teacher
script.text: Next, draw a simple design along one side. Do not colour it yet.

script.speaker: Teacher
script.text: Then colour your design carefully, keeping inside the lines.

script.speaker: Teacher
script.text: After that, make a small hole at the top with a pencil point.

script.speaker: Teacher
script.text: Finally, thread a piece of ribbon through the hole and tie a knot. Your bookmark is ready.

questions.prompt: Put the steps in the order the teacher gives them.
items: Make a hole at the top
questions.explanation: The teacher uses First, Next, Then, After that and Finally to mark the five steps in order.

questions.prompt: Complete the notes about the strip of card.
questions.explanation: The strip is about twenty centimetres long and five centimetres wide.

questions.prompt: Match each material to what it is used for.
questions.explanation: Each material has one clear use in the instructions.

questions.prompt: What are students told NOT to do when they draw the design?
questions.explanation: The teacher says, 'Do not colour it yet.'

questions.prompt: What is used to make the hole?
questions.explanation: The teacher says to make a small hole with a pencil point.

questions.prompt: What is the last thing you do?
options: Tie a knot in the ribbon
questions.explanation: Finally, you thread the ribbon through and tie a knot.

tests.title: A telephone call about a lost bag
tests.description: A caller reports a lost bag to an office. Competency level 3.3: listens to a simple text for specific information.
tests.instructions: Listen to the telephone call and note the details. Answer the questions, then submit.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Listen to a telephone call to a bus depot office.

script.speaker: Officer
script.text: Good evening, lost property office. How may I help you?

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Good evening. I think I left my bag on the number one hundred and thirty eight bus this afternoon.

script.speaker: Officer
script.text: I see. Can you describe the bag?

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: It is a dark blue backpack with a broken zip on the front pocket.

script.speaker: Officer
script.text: And what was inside it?

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Two school books, a lunch box and a pair of spectacles in a brown case.

script.speaker: Officer
script.text: We do have a blue backpack here. Please come tomorrow morning after nine and bring your identity card.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Thank you so much. I will come at half past nine.

questions.prompt: Complete the lost property record.
questions.explanation: The caller lost a dark blue backpack on the number 138 bus.

questions.prompt: What is wrong with the bag?
options: A broken zip on the front pocket
questions.explanation: The caller says it has a broken zip on the front pocket.

questions.prompt: Match each item to where it was or what it looked like.
questions.explanation: The bag held two school books, a lunch box and spectacles in a brown case. The identity card must be brought to collect the bag.

questions.prompt: At what time will the caller come?
questions.explanation: The caller says, 'I will come at half past nine.'

questions.prompt: What must the caller bring to collect the bag?
questions.explanation: The officer asks the caller to bring an identity card.

questions.prompt: Complete: Besides books and spectacles, the bag contained a ____ box.
questions.explanation: The caller lists two school books, a lunch box and spectacles.

tests.title: Library rules
tests.description: The librarian explains how the school library works. Competency levels 3.3 and 3.4: listens for specific information and transfers it into other forms.
tests.instructions: Listen to the librarian and complete the notes. Answer the questions, then submit.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Listen to a librarian speaking to new students.

script.speaker: Librarian
script.text: Welcome to the school library. Let me explain a few simple rules.

script.speaker: Librarian
script.text: Each student may borrow two books at a time. You may keep them for fourteen days.

script.speaker: Librarian
script.text: If a book is returned late, there is a small fine of five rupees for each day.

script.speaker: Librarian
script.text: Reference books, such as dictionaries and atlases, may be used here but cannot be taken home.

script.speaker: Librarian
script.text: The library is open from seven thirty in the morning until four in the afternoon, Monday to Friday.

script.speaker: Librarian
script.text: Please keep your voices low, and never write in a library book.

questions.prompt: Complete the notes about borrowing.
questions.explanation: Two books, for fourteen days, with a five rupee fine for each day a book is late.

questions.prompt: Which books may NOT be taken home?
questions.explanation: Reference books such as dictionaries and atlases may be used in the library but not taken home.

questions.prompt: Complete the notes about opening hours.
questions.explanation: The library opens at seven thirty in the morning and closes at four in the afternoon.

questions.prompt: On which days is the library open?
questions.explanation: The librarian says Monday to Friday.

questions.prompt: Match each item to the rule that applies to it.

pairs.meaning: Use it in the library only
A fine of five rupees a day

questions.explanation: Each rule in the talk applies to one of these.

questions.prompt: What are students asked to do about their voices?
questions.explanation: The librarian asks students to keep their voices low.

tests.title: The weather report
tests.description: A radio weather forecast for several regions. Competency level 3.4: listens and transfers the needed information into other forms.
tests.instructions: Listen to the forecast and fill in the weather chart. Answer the questions, then submit.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Listen to a weather forecast on the radio.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: Good morning. Here is the weather forecast for today, the ninth of June.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: In the Western Province, heavy showers are expected in the afternoon. Please carry an umbrella.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: The Central Province will be misty in the early morning, but the sky will clear by midday.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: In the Northern Province the day will be dry and hot, with temperatures reaching thirty four degrees.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: Strong winds are expected along the southern coast, so fishermen are advised not to go out to sea.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: That is all for now. The next forecast will be broadcast at one o'clock.

questions.prompt: Complete the weather chart.
questions.explanation: Heavy showers in the west, mist in the central hills, and thirty four degrees in the north.

questions.prompt: When will the Central Province sky clear?
questions.explanation: The presenter says the sky will clear by midday.

questions.prompt: Why are fishermen advised not to go out to sea?
questions.explanation: Strong winds are expected along the southern coast.

questions.prompt: What are people in the Western Province advised to carry?
questions.explanation: The presenter says, 'Please carry an umbrella.'

questions.prompt: Match each region to its weather.
questions.explanation: Each region is given one distinct kind of weather in the forecast.

questions.prompt: Complete: The next forecast will be broadcast at ____ o'clock.
questions.explanation: The presenter says the next forecast is at one o'clock.

tests.title: At the dentist
tests.description: A dentist gives a patient advice and instructions. Competency level 3.2: listens and follows instructions and responds to requests.
tests.instructions: Listen to the conversation and follow the advice given. Answer the questions, then submit.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Listen to a conversation at a dental clinic.

script.speaker: Dentist
script.text: Good afternoon, Menaka. How long have you had this pain?

script.speaker: Menaka
script.text: For about five days, doctor. It becomes worse when I drink something cold.

script.speaker: Dentist
script.text: I see. One of your back teeth has a small cavity. It must be filled.

script.speaker: Menaka
script.text: Will it hurt?

script.speaker: Dentist
script.text: No. The area will be numbed first, so you will feel almost nothing.

script.speaker: Dentist
script.text: After the filling, do not eat anything for one hour. Avoid very hot and very cold drinks for two days.

script.speaker: Dentist
script.text: Brush twice a day, and come back in six months for a check-up.

script.speaker: Menaka
script.text: Thank you, doctor. I will remember all of that.

questions.prompt: How long has Menaka had the pain?
questions.explanation: She says she has had it for about five days.

questions.prompt: What makes the pain worse?
questions.explanation: She says it becomes worse when she drinks something cold.

questions.prompt: Put the dentist's instructions in the order he gives them.
items: Do not eat for one hour
Avoid very hot and very cold drinks for two days
questions.explanation: The dentist gives these four instructions in this order after explaining the filling.

questions.prompt: Complete the patient's card.
questions.explanation: A small cavity must be filled; no eating for one hour; a check-up in six months.

questions.prompt: Why does the dentist say it will not hurt?
questions.explanation: The dentist says the area will be numbed first, so she will feel almost nothing.

questions.prompt: Complete: The tooth with the cavity is one of her ____ teeth.
questions.explanation: The dentist says one of her back teeth has a small cavity.

tests.title: How paper is made
tests.description: A short explanation of a process, told in the passive voice. Competency levels 3.3 and 3.4, and competency level 6.1, the passive voice in simple tenses.
tests.instructions: Listen to the explanation of how paper is made. Put the stages in order and answer the questions, then submit.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Listen to a talk about how paper is made.

script.speaker: Speaker
script.text: Have you ever wondered how paper is made? The process is simpler than most people think.

script.speaker: Speaker
script.text: First, trees are cut down and the logs are taken to a factory.

script.speaker: Speaker
script.text: At the factory, the bark is removed and the wood is chopped into very small chips.

script.speaker: Speaker
script.text: The chips are then mixed with water and chemicals until a soft grey pulp is formed.

script.speaker: Speaker
script.text: The pulp is spread onto a wide moving screen, where most of the water drains away.

script.speaker: Speaker
script.text: Finally, the sheet is pressed and dried, and the paper is rolled up ready to be cut.

script.speaker: Speaker
script.text: Today, a great deal of paper is also made from waste paper that has been collected and cleaned.

questions.prompt: Put the stages of paper making in order.
items: The chips are mixed with water and chemicals
The pulp is spread on a screen
The sheet is pressed and dried
questions.explanation: The talk moves through these five stages in order, each described in the passive voice.

questions.prompt: Complete: At the factory, the ____ is removed from the logs.
questions.explanation: The speaker says the bark is removed and the wood is chopped into chips.

questions.prompt: What is mixed with the wood chips?
questions.explanation: The chips are mixed with water and chemicals to form pulp.

questions.prompt: What colour is the pulp?
questions.explanation: The talk describes a soft grey pulp.

questions.prompt: What happens on the wide moving screen?
options: Most of the water drains away
questions.explanation: The pulp is spread onto the screen, where most of the water drains away.

questions.prompt: What else is paper made from today?
questions.explanation: The speaker says a great deal of paper is also made from waste paper that has been collected and cleaned.

tests.title: A report on the school garden
tests.description: A student reports to the class on a project. Competency level 3.3: listens to a text for specific information.
tests.instructions: Listen to the report and note the details. Answer the questions, then submit.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Listen to a student reporting on a school project.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: Good morning. I am going to report on our school garden project, which began in January.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: Twenty two students from Grade eight took part. We were given a small plot behind the science room.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: In the first month the soil was dug and cleared. It was very hard work because the ground had not been used for years.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: We then planted tomatoes, beans and a row of chillies.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: Unfortunately, the tomatoes were eaten by insects, so we had to plant them a second time.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: By April we had harvested nearly six kilograms of beans, which were given to the school kitchen.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: Next term we hope to add a compost bin so that nothing is wasted.

questions.prompt: Complete the project record.
questions.explanation: The project began in January with twenty two students and produced nearly six kilograms of beans.

questions.prompt: Where is the garden plot?
questions.explanation: The student says they were given a small plot behind the science room.

questions.prompt: Why did the students have to plant tomatoes twice?
options: The first plants were eaten by insects
questions.explanation: The tomatoes were eaten by insects, so they were planted a second time.

questions.prompt: Put the stages of the project in order.
items: The soil was dug and cleared
Tomatoes, beans and chillies were planted
The tomatoes were eaten by insects
questions.explanation: The report follows this order from January through to April.

questions.prompt: Who received the beans?
questions.explanation: The beans were given to the school kitchen.

questions.prompt: Complete: Next term they hope to add a ____ bin.
questions.explanation: The student says they hope to add a compost bin so that nothing is wasted.

tests.title: Booking the community hall
tests.description: A caller arranges to hire a hall. Competency level 3.4: listens and transfers the needed information into other forms.
tests.instructions: Listen to the conversation and complete the booking form. Answer the questions, then submit.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Listen to a telephone conversation about hiring a hall.

script.speaker: Clerk
script.text: Good morning, community hall office.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Good morning. I would like to book the hall for a music competition.

script.speaker: Clerk
script.text: Certainly. On what date?

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Saturday the fifteenth of November, from two in the afternoon until six.

script.speaker: Clerk
script.text: That is four hours. The charge is one thousand five hundred rupees for each hour.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: And is a deposit required?

script.speaker: Clerk
script.text: Yes. Half of the total must be paid when the booking is made, and the rest on the day.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: I understand. My name is Fathima Rizwan, and my number is zero seven seven, four five six, seven eight nine zero.

script.speaker: Clerk
script.text: Thank you. The hall will be held for you until Friday.

questions.prompt: Complete the booking form.
questions.explanation: The booking is for Saturday the fifteenth of November, two until six, in the name of Fathima Rizwan.

questions.prompt: For how many hours is the hall booked?
questions.explanation: From two until six is four hours, as the clerk confirms.

questions.prompt: What is the charge for each hour?
questions.explanation: The clerk says one thousand five hundred rupees for each hour.

questions.prompt: How much must be paid when the booking is made?
questions.explanation: Half of the total is paid at booking and the rest on the day.

questions.prompt: What is the hall being used for?
questions.explanation: The caller says she wants to book the hall for a music competition.

questions.prompt: Complete: The hall will be held for the caller until ____.
questions.explanation: The clerk says the hall will be held until Friday.

tests.title: An interview with a wildlife officer
tests.description: A radio interview about elephants and farmland. Competency levels 3.3 and 3.4: listens for specific information and transfers it into other forms.
tests.instructions: Listen to the interview and complete the notes. Answer the questions, then submit.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Listen to a radio interview with a wildlife officer.

script.speaker: Interviewer
script.text: Mr Bandara, you have worked with elephants for many years. What is the biggest problem today?

script.speaker: Officer
script.text: The biggest problem is that the forest is shrinking. Elephants need a great deal of space, and that space is being taken for farming and building.

script.speaker: Interviewer
script.text: And what happens when an elephant enters a village?

script.speaker: Officer
script.text: Usually it is looking for food. Crops are easier to find than wild plants, so the animal returns again and again.

script.speaker: Interviewer
script.text: What is being done about it?

script.speaker: Officer
script.text: Electric fences have been put up around several villages, and they work well when they are properly maintained. The difficulty is that many are not.

script.speaker: Interviewer
script.text: Is there anything the villagers themselves can do?

script.speaker: Officer
script.text: Yes. Growing crops that elephants dislike, such as citrus and chillies, has helped in some districts. But it takes patience, and results are not seen in a single season.

questions.prompt: Complete the notes on the interview.
questions.explanation: The forest is shrinking; elephants come for food; citrus and chillies are crops they dislike.

questions.prompt: Why is the forest getting smaller?
options: Because land is taken for farming and building
Because of disease in the trees
questions.explanation: The officer says the space is being taken for farming and building.

questions.prompt: Why do electric fences often fail?
options: Elephants are not afraid of them
questions.explanation: The officer says they work well when properly maintained, but many are not.

questions.prompt: Why does an elephant return to a village again and again?
answer: crops are easier to find than wild plants
because crops are easy to find
questions.explanation: Crops are easier to find than wild plants, so the animal comes back.

questions.prompt: What does the officer suggest about the crop solution?
options: It needs patience and takes more than one season
It is too expensive for villagers
questions.explanation: He says it takes patience and results are not seen in a single season.

questions.prompt: Complete: Electric ____ have been put up around several villages.
questions.explanation: The officer says electric fences have been put up around several villages.

tests.title: Making plans for Saturday
tests.description: Two friends discuss what to do, without stating everything directly. Competency levels 5.7 and 5.8: infers ellipted information and infers implied information.
tests.instructions: Listen carefully. Some things are suggested rather than said. Answer the questions, then submit.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Listen to two friends making plans.

script.speaker: Ishara
script.text: So, Saturday. The new film starts at four.

script.speaker: Ravindu
script.text: Four. Hmm.

script.speaker: Ishara
script.text: You do not sound very keen.

script.speaker: Ravindu
script.text: No, no, it is fine. It is just that my cousin's almsgiving is at eleven, and these things never finish when they say they will.

script.speaker: Ishara
script.text: Ah. Then perhaps the six o'clock show instead?

script.speaker: Ravindu
script.text: That would be safer. Although then I would have to leave straight after, because of the last bus.

script.speaker: Ishara
script.text: You could stay at my place. My mother would be glad; she has been asking after you since the examinations.

script.speaker: Ravindu
script.text: Has she? Then that settles it. Six o'clock.

questions.prompt: Why is Ravindu unsure about the four o'clock show?
options: He does not like the film
He may still be at the almsgiving
questions.explanation: He says the almsgiving is at eleven and 'these things never finish when they say they will', implying he may not be free by four.

questions.prompt: What does 'Four. Hmm.' suggest about Ravindu's feelings?
options: He has a difficulty he has not yet explained
questions.explanation: The short reply and Ishara's response, 'You do not sound very keen', show hesitation before he gives his reason.

questions.prompt: What problem would Ravindu have after the six o'clock show?
answer: he would miss the last bus
questions.explanation: He says he would have to leave straight after because of the last bus.

questions.prompt: Why does Ishara mention her mother?
options: To make staying overnight sound welcome
To warn him her mother is strict
questions.explanation: She offers her place to stay and adds that her mother would be glad, which removes his objection politely.

questions.prompt: What have the friends finally agreed to do?
options: Go to the four o'clock show
Go to the six o'clock show
questions.explanation: Ravindu ends with 'Then that settles it. Six o'clock.'

questions.prompt: What is implied by 'Has she?'
options: Ravindu is pleased and a little surprised
questions.explanation: He immediately agrees afterwards, so the short question shows pleased surprise, not doubt.

tests.title: A young athlete is interviewed
tests.description: A school athlete answers questions after a competition. Competency levels 3.3 and 3.4: listens for specific information and transfers it into other forms.
tests.instructions: Listen to the interview and complete the record card. Answer the questions, then submit.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Listen to an interview after a school athletics meet.

script.speaker: Reporter
script.text: Congratulations, Thilini. You have just won the eight hundred metres. How does it feel?

script.speaker: Thilini
script.text: Thank you. It still does not feel real. My time was two minutes and nineteen seconds, which is my best so far.

script.speaker: Reporter
script.text: How long have you been training?

script.speaker: Thilini
script.text: Three years. I began when I was in Grade six, though I only started training seriously last year.

script.speaker: Reporter
script.text: What does a normal week look like?

script.speaker: Thilini
script.text: I run five mornings a week before school, and on Saturdays I do exercises for strength. Sunday is a rest day.

script.speaker: Reporter
script.text: Has it been difficult with school work?

script.speaker: Thilini
script.text: It was, at first. My teachers were worried that my marks would fall. But I learnt to do my homework earlier in the evening, and now it is manageable.

script.speaker: Reporter
script.text: And what is next?

script.speaker: Thilini
script.text: The provincial meet in August. I have been told that the qualifying time is two minutes fifteen, so I have work to do.

questions.prompt: Complete the athlete's record card.
questions.explanation: She won the eight hundred metres in two minutes nineteen, after three years of training.

questions.prompt: When did Thilini begin running?
questions.explanation: She began in Grade six, though she only started training seriously last year.

questions.prompt: Match each day to what she does.
questions.explanation: She runs five mornings a week, does strength work on Saturdays and rests on Sunday.

questions.prompt: What were her teachers worried about?
questions.explanation: She says her teachers were worried that her marks would fall.

questions.prompt: How did she solve the problem with school work?
answer: doing homework earlier in the evening
questions.explanation: She learnt to do her homework earlier in the evening.

questions.prompt: Complete: The qualifying time for the provincial meet is two minutes ____.
questions.explanation: She says she has been told the qualifying time is two minutes fifteen.

tests.title: At the bus halt
tests.description: A short scene in which feelings are shown rather than stated. Competency level 5.8: infers implied information.
tests.instructions: Listen carefully to what is said and to what is left unsaid. Answer the questions, then submit.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Listen to a conversation at a bus halt.

script.speaker: Kumudu
script.text: You are up early.

script.speaker: Anura
script.text: Interview.

script.speaker: Kumudu
script.text: Ah. The one at the bank?

script.speaker: Anura
script.text: The third one at the bank.

script.speaker: Kumudu
script.text: Well. Third time is the charm, they say.

script.speaker: Anura
script.text: They say a great many things. I have pressed this shirt twice.

script.speaker: Kumudu
script.text: It looks very smart.

script.speaker: Anura
script.text: Does it? Good. My sister said the collar was crooked, and now I cannot stop thinking about the collar.

script.speaker: Kumudu
script.text: Your bus is coming. Nobody will be looking at your collar, Anura.

questions.prompt: How many times has Anura been interviewed at the bank?
questions.explanation: He corrects Kumudu with 'The third one at the bank', so this is his third interview there.

questions.prompt: What does 'They say a great many things' suggest about Anura's mood?
options: He is impatient with easy encouragement
questions.explanation: He dismisses the proverb, which shows he is too anxious to be comforted by a saying.

questions.prompt: What detail shows that Anura is nervous about his appearance?
answer: he has pressed the shirt twice
he cannot stop thinking about the collar
questions.explanation: Pressing one shirt twice, and being unable to stop thinking about the collar, both show nervousness.

questions.prompt: Why does Anura keep thinking about the collar?
options: His sister said it was crooked
questions.explanation: He says his sister said the collar was crooked, and now he cannot stop thinking about it.

questions.prompt: What is Kumudu trying to do in the last line?
questions.explanation: Saying nobody will be looking at his collar is meant to calm him before he boards.

questions.prompt: Which word best describes Anura in this scene?
questions.explanation: The short replies, the twice-pressed shirt and the worry about the collar all point to anxiety.

tests.title: A talk on saving water
tests.description: A short talk with facts and advice. Competency levels 3.4 and 3.6: transfers information into other forms and reports information.
tests.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete the notes. Answer the questions, then submit.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Listen to a talk given at a school assembly.

script.speaker: Speaker
script.text: Good morning. I want to talk about something we all use and rarely think about: water.

script.speaker: Speaker
script.text: A tap left running while you brush your teeth wastes about six litres a minute.

script.speaker: Speaker
script.text: A dripping tap may seem harmless, but it can waste as much as fifteen litres in a single day.

script.speaker: Speaker
script.text: Here is what you can do. Turn the tap off while brushing. Report any leaking tap to the office at once.

script.speaker: Speaker
script.text: Water the school garden in the early morning or late evening, because in the middle of the day most of it simply evaporates.

script.speaker: Speaker
script.text: None of these actions is difficult. Together, though, they would save this school thousands of litres every term.

questions.prompt: Complete the notes on water waste.
questions.explanation: A running tap wastes about six litres a minute; a dripping tap up to fifteen litres a day.

questions.prompt: Put the speaker's three pieces of advice in the order they are given.
items: Turn the tap off while brushing
Report leaking taps to the office
Water the garden early or late
questions.explanation: The advice is given in this order after the two facts about waste.

questions.prompt: Why should the garden not be watered at midday?
options: The plants are damaged by heat
questions.explanation: The speaker says most of it simply evaporates in the middle of the day.

questions.prompt: What should you do if you find a leaking tap?
answer: report any leaking tap to the office
questions.explanation: The speaker says to report any leaking tap to the office at once.

questions.prompt: What is the speaker's main point at the end?
options: Small actions together save a great deal
The school wastes too much money
Students do not care about water
questions.explanation: None of the actions is difficult, but together they would save thousands of litres every term.

questions.prompt: Complete: Together these actions would save thousands of litres every ____.
questions.explanation: The speaker ends by saying thousands of litres every term.

tests.title: A presentation on plastic waste
tests.description: A structured talk to be summarised in note form. Competency level 3.8: takes notes from oral presentations.
tests.instructions: Listen to the presentation and take notes as you listen. Complete the note frame and answer the questions, then submit.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Listen to a student presentation on plastic waste.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: Good afternoon. My presentation has three parts: the scale of the problem, its causes, and what can realistically be done.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: Firstly, the scale. It has been estimated that a single family in this town throws away about four kilograms of plastic every week.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: Secondly, the causes. Most of that plastic has been used only once. Packaging, shopping bags and water bottles account for the greater part of it.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: However, blaming shoppers alone would be unfair, since very few products are sold without packaging in the first place.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: Thirdly, solutions. Cloth bags are the obvious step, but they are only effective if they are actually carried. A bag left at home helps nobody.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: Furthermore, if refill stations had been introduced ten years ago, a great deal of this waste would have been avoided.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: In conclusion, the problem is large but not hopeless. Small habits, repeated daily, are worth more than one grand gesture.

questions.prompt: Complete the note frame for this presentation.
questions.explanation: The talk has three parts; a family throws away about four kilograms a week; cloth bags are the obvious step.

questions.prompt: Put the three parts of the presentation in the order announced.
questions.explanation: The presenter announces the order at the start and follows it with Firstly, Secondly and Thirdly.

questions.prompt: Which three things account for most of the plastic?
options: Packaging, shopping bags and water bottles
questions.explanation: The presenter names packaging, shopping bags and water bottles.

questions.prompt: Why does the presenter say blaming shoppers alone would be unfair?
options: Very few products are sold without packaging
Shoppers are not told about the problem
questions.explanation: Very few products are sold without packaging in the first place, so the choice is not entirely the shopper's.

questions.prompt: What does the presenter mean by 'A bag left at home helps nobody'?
options: A solution only works if it is actually used
Bags should be stored at home
questions.explanation: Cloth bags are effective only if they are carried, so the habit matters as much as the object.

questions.prompt: According to the conclusion, what is worth more than one grand gesture?
questions.explanation: The final line says small habits, repeated daily, are worth more than one grand gesture.

tests.title: A discussion about school uniforms
tests.description: Three speakers put different views. Competency level 3.6: listens and reports information.
tests.instructions: Listen to the discussion and follow who says what. Answer the questions, then submit.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Listen to three students discussing school uniforms.

script.speaker: Chair
script.text: Our topic today is whether school uniforms should be compulsory. Dinesh, your view first.

script.speaker: Dinesh
script.text: I am in favour. A uniform hides the difference between a rich family and a poor one. Without it, some students would be judged every morning by what they were wearing.

script.speaker: Chair
script.text: Hasini?

script.speaker: Hasini
script.text: I disagree, though not entirely. My objection is not to uniforms but to the way the rule is enforced. Students are punished for the length of a sleeve while nobody asks whether they have eaten.

script.speaker: Chair
script.text: Nuwan, you have been quiet.

script.speaker: Nuwan
script.text: I can see both sides. On the one hand, Dinesh is right that a uniform levels things. On the other hand, Hasini is right that the rule is often applied without thought. Perhaps the uniform should stay and the punishments should go.

script.speaker: Chair
script.text: So we have agreement on the principle and disagreement on the practice. Thank you all.

questions.prompt: Match each speaker to the view they express.

pairs.meaning: The problem is how the rule is enforced
Keep the uniform but drop the punishments

questions.explanation: Each speaker takes a distinct position, which the chair sums up at the end.

questions.prompt: What is Hasini's objection?
options: The rule is enforced without thought for bigger problems
questions.explanation: She says students are punished for the length of a sleeve while nobody asks whether they have eaten.

questions.prompt: Which phrases show Nuwan is balancing two views?
options: On the one hand and on the other hand
questions.explanation: On the one hand and on the other hand are the discourse markers used to weigh two sides.

questions.prompt: According to Dinesh, what would happen without uniforms?
answer: students would be judged by what they wear
some students would be judged by their clothes
students would be judged every morning by what they were wearing
they would be judged by clothes
questions.explanation: He says some students would be judged every morning by what they were wearing.

questions.prompt: How does the chair sum up the discussion?
options: Agreement on the principle, disagreement on the practice
questions.explanation: The chair says there is agreement on the principle and disagreement on the practice.

questions.prompt: What does Hasini mean by 'I disagree, though not entirely'?
options: She agrees with everything Dinesh said
She rejects only part of the argument
She wants to change the topic
questions.explanation: She goes on to say her objection is not to uniforms themselves but to how the rule is enforced.

tests.title: A news report on the floods
tests.description: A radio news bulletin with figures and instructions. Competency levels 3.4 and 3.6: transfers information into other forms and reports information.
tests.instructions: Listen to the bulletin and complete the report summary. Answer the questions, then submit.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Listen to a radio news bulletin.

script.speaker: Newsreader
script.text: Heavy rain has continued for a third day in the Ratnapura district, and several low-lying areas have been flooded.

script.speaker: Newsreader
script.text: According to the Disaster Management Centre, about two thousand four hundred families have been affected.

script.speaker: Newsreader
script.text: Eleven schools have been closed and are being used as temporary shelters.

script.speaker: Newsreader
script.text: The main road to Balangoda has been blocked by a landslide since yesterday evening. Engineers say it will be cleared within two days.

script.speaker: Newsreader
script.text: Residents have been advised not to cross flowing water, even where it appears shallow.

script.speaker: Newsreader
script.text: Meanwhile, relief supplies are being distributed from the divisional secretariat, and a helpline has been opened.

questions.prompt: Complete the news summary.
questions.explanation: About two thousand four hundred families in the Ratnapura district are affected and eleven schools have closed.

questions.prompt: What are the closed schools being used for?
questions.explanation: The bulletin says they are being used as temporary shelters.

questions.prompt: Why is the main road to Balangoda blocked?
questions.explanation: The road has been blocked by a landslide since yesterday evening.

questions.prompt: How long will it take to clear the road?
questions.explanation: Engineers say it will be cleared within two days.

questions.prompt: What warning is given to residents?
questions.explanation: Residents are advised not to cross flowing water, even where it appears shallow.

questions.prompt: Complete: Relief supplies are being distributed from the divisional ____.
questions.explanation: The bulletin says supplies are being distributed from the divisional secretariat.

tests.title: Signposts in a talk
tests.description: A talk in which the linking words carry the structure. Competency level 3.7: recognizes discourse markers.
tests.instructions: Listen to how the speaker signals each new idea. Answer the questions about those signals, then submit.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Listen to a short talk about learning a language.

script.speaker: Speaker
script.text: People often ask me how long it takes to learn English. To begin with, that is the wrong question.

script.speaker: Speaker
script.text: The right question is what you want to do with it. For example, ordering a meal and writing a report are not the same skill at all.

script.speaker: Speaker
script.text: Moreover, the two are learnt in different ways. One is picked up by speaking; the other has to be studied.

script.speaker: Speaker
script.text: Nevertheless, both improve with the same habit: daily use, even for ten minutes.

script.speaker: Speaker
script.text: On the other hand, daily use alone is not enough if the same mistakes are repeated. Correction matters.

script.speaker: Speaker
script.text: To sum up, decide what you need, practise it daily, and let someone correct you.

questions.prompt: Match each signal word to what it tells the listener.
questions.explanation: Each marker tells the listener what kind of idea is coming next, before the idea itself arrives.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say is the wrong question?
options: What you want to do with English
How long it takes to learn English
questions.explanation: The speaker says 'how long does it take' is the wrong question.

questions.prompt: Which two activities are given as an example of different skills?
options: Ordering a meal and writing a report
questions.explanation: The speaker contrasts ordering a meal with writing a report.

questions.prompt: What idea does 'On the other hand' introduce here?
options: A further reason to practise daily
questions.explanation: It introduces the point that daily use is not enough if the same mistakes are repeated.

questions.prompt: Put the speaker's three final pieces of advice in order.
questions.explanation: The closing summary gives the three in this order.

questions.prompt: Complete: Both skills improve with daily use, even for ____ minutes.
questions.explanation: The speaker says daily use, even for ten minutes.

tests.title: A staff room conversation
tests.description: Two teachers work through a timetable problem. Competency levels 3.3 and 5.8: listens for specific information and infers what is implied.
tests.instructions: Listen to the conversation and follow the problem being solved. Answer the questions, then submit.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Listen to two teachers in a staff room.

script.speaker: Mrs Perera
script.text: Have you seen the new timetable? I have Grade ten for English on Friday, last period.

script.speaker: Mr Jayasuriya
script.text: Ah. The graveyard slot.

script.speaker: Mrs Perera
script.text: Exactly. They have had double mathematics before it, and by then nothing goes in.

script.speaker: Mr Jayasuriya
script.text: Could you swap? I have them Wednesday morning for geography.

script.speaker: Mrs Perera
script.text: That would be ideal, but the timetable was finalised last week. If we had spoken to the principal before the meeting, it would have been changed easily.

script.speaker: Mr Jayasuriya
script.text: It may still be possible. She has been known to make small adjustments, if both teachers agree in writing.

script.speaker: Mrs Perera
script.text: Then I shall write this evening. It is worth trying. The alternative is a whole term of Friday afternoons.

questions.prompt: What does Mr Jayasuriya mean by 'the graveyard slot'?
options: A lesson nobody is timetabled for
The last period, when students are least alert
The first period of the day
questions.explanation: It is his name for Friday last period, and Mrs Perera agrees that by then nothing goes in.

questions.prompt: Why is that period especially difficult?
options: The students have had double mathematics before it
questions.explanation: She says they have had double mathematics before it.

questions.prompt: What subject does Mr Jayasuriya teach the same class?
questions.explanation: He says he has them Wednesday morning for geography.

questions.prompt: What does the sentence beginning 'If we had spoken to the principal…' tell you?
options: They did speak to her and it worked
They did not speak to her in time
They will speak to her tomorrow
questions.explanation: It is a Type 3 conditional, describing something that did not happen. They did not speak to her before the meeting.

questions.prompt: On what condition might the principal still change the timetable?
options: If both teachers agree in writing
If the term has not begun
If there is a free room
questions.explanation: He says she has been known to make small adjustments if both teachers agree in writing.

questions.prompt: What does Mrs Perera decide to do?
options: Write to the principal that evening
questions.explanation: She says, 'Then I shall write this evening. It is worth trying.'

tests.title: A debate: has social media helped or harmed young people?
tests.description: Two speakers argue opposing cases before a chairperson. Competency levels 3.6 and 8.16: listens and reports information, and follows a debate.
tests.instructions: Listen to the debate and follow each speaker's argument. Answer the questions, then submit.

script.speaker: Chair
script.text: The motion is that social media has done more harm than good to young people. Speaking for the motion, Nilanka.

script.speaker: Nilanka
script.text: Thank you. My case rests on one word: attention. A generation has been trained to expect something new every few seconds.

script.speaker: Nilanka
script.text: Reading a chapter, sitting an examination, listening to a teacher: all of these require the very thing that these applications are designed to break.

script.speaker: Nilanka
script.text: I am not claiming that young people are foolish. I am claiming that they are being acted upon by companies with far greater resources than they have.

script.speaker: Chair
script.text: Speaking against the motion, Ashen.

script.speaker: Ashen
script.text: My friend describes young people as if they were clay. They are not. The same platforms he condemns have taught thousands of students to code, to draw and to speak a second language.

script.speaker: Ashen
script.text: Moreover, the harm he describes is not new. The same was said of television, and of the novel before it.

script.speaker: Ashen
script.text: What has genuinely changed is that a student in a distant village now has the same library as a student in Colombo. I would not surrender that lightly.

script.speaker: Chair
script.text: Thank you both. The house will now vote.

questions.prompt: On what single idea does Nilanka rest his case?
questions.explanation: He says, 'My case rests on one word: attention.'

questions.prompt: What does Nilanka say he is NOT claiming?
questions.explanation: He explicitly says he is not claiming that young people are foolish, only that they are being acted upon.

questions.prompt: What does Ashen mean by 'as if they were clay'?
options: That young people are shaped passively, with no will of their own
questions.explanation: He is objecting that Nilanka's argument treats young people as things moulded by others rather than as people who choose.

questions.prompt: Match each speaker to the argument they make.

pairs.meaning: The applications are designed to break concentration
The same fears were expressed about television and the novel

questions.explanation: Nilanka argues from attention; Ashen argues that the alarm is not new.

questions.prompt: According to Ashen, what has genuinely changed?
answer: a student in a village has the same library as a student in colombo
students everywhere have the same library
questions.explanation: He says a student in a distant village now has the same library as a student in Colombo.

questions.prompt: Which best describes the structure of this debate?
options: One states a harm, the other disputes both the harm and its novelty
The chair gives the main argument
questions.explanation: Nilanka argues harm; Ashen disputes the harm and adds that such fears are not new.

tests.title: A careers talk
tests.description: An extended talk to be summarised in note form. Competency level 3.8: takes notes from oral presentations.
tests.instructions: Listen and take notes as the speaker moves through each section. Complete the note frame and answer the questions, then submit.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Listen to a careers talk given to Grade eleven students.

script.speaker: Speaker
script.text: Good morning. I have been asked to speak about choosing a path after the Ordinary Level examination. I shall cover three things: streams, timing, and a mistake I see every year.

script.speaker: Speaker
script.text: First, streams. You will choose between science, commerce, arts and technology. Each opens some doors and closes others, but far fewer than students imagine.

script.speaker: Speaker
script.text: Secondly, timing. Applications for most Advanced Level classes close in the third week of January. If you wait for your results before enquiring, you will already be late.

script.speaker: Speaker
script.text: Thirdly, the mistake. Every year, students choose a stream because a friend has chosen it. Within one term, one of the two is unhappy, and it is usually the follower.

script.speaker: Speaker
script.text: Consequently, my advice is this: write down what you actually enjoy doing for two hours without being told to. That list is more useful than any ranking of subjects.

script.speaker: Speaker
script.text: Finally, do speak to somebody already doing the course. Prospectuses describe what a subject should be. A student will tell you what it is.

questions.prompt: Complete the note frame.

lines.label: The common mistake:
answer: choosing a stream because a friend chose it

questions.explanation: Three sections; applications close in the third week of January; the mistake is following a friend's choice.

questions.prompt: Put the three announced sections in order.
questions.explanation: The speaker announces this order at the start and follows it with First, Secondly and Thirdly.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about the doors a stream closes?
options: It closes far fewer than students imagine
It closes no doors at all
questions.explanation: Each stream opens some doors and closes others, but far fewer than students imagine.

questions.prompt: Why should students not wait for their results before enquiring?
questions.explanation: Applications close in the third week of January, so waiting makes a student late.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker advise students to write down?
answer: what you enjoy doing for two hours without being told to
what you enjoy for two hours
questions.explanation: He advises writing down what you actually enjoy doing for two hours without being told to.

questions.prompt: What is the difference the speaker draws between a prospectus and a student?
options: One is free, the other is not
A prospectus says what a subject should be; a student says what it is
A student knows the examination better

tests.title: An interview with a writer
tests.description: A longer interview in which much is implied. Competency levels 5.7 and 5.8: infers ellipted and implied information.
tests.instructions: Listen carefully. Several answers depend on what is suggested rather than stated. Answer the questions, then submit.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Listen to an interview with a novelist.

script.speaker: Interviewer
script.text: Your first novel took eleven years. The second took nine months. What changed?

script.speaker: Writer
script.text: I stopped waiting to feel ready.

script.speaker: Interviewer
script.text: That sounds simple.

script.speaker: Writer
script.text: It is simple. It is not easy. For eleven years I believed that a better version of myself would one day sit down and write the book. He never arrived, and I got tired of waiting for him.

script.speaker: Interviewer
script.text: Some critics have called the second novel rushed.

script.speaker: Writer
script.text: Some critics called the first one overworked. One learns to hold both remarks loosely.

script.speaker: Interviewer
script.text: Do you read your reviews?

script.speaker: Writer
script.text: I read them the way one presses a bruise. Knowing better does not stop you.

script.speaker: Interviewer
script.text: And the third book?

script.speaker: Writer
script.text: It is being written. Slowly, but it is being written, which is a different thing from being planned.

questions.prompt: What does the writer say changed between the two novels?
options: He stopped waiting to feel ready
He moved to a quieter house
questions.explanation: His answer is direct: 'I stopped waiting to feel ready.'

questions.prompt: What does 'He never arrived' refer to?
options: The better version of himself he was waiting to become
questions.explanation: He describes believing a better version of himself would one day write the book, and that person never came.

questions.prompt: What does the writer imply by mentioning that critics called the first novel overworked?
options: The critics were right about both books
Opposite criticisms cancel out, so neither should be taken too seriously
He agrees the second was rushed
questions.explanation: He follows it with 'One learns to hold both remarks loosely', suggesting contradictory criticism should not be weighted heavily.

questions.prompt: What does 'I read them the way one presses a bruise' tell you?
options: He reads them knowing it will hurt, and cannot stop
questions.explanation: Pressing a bruise is deliberately causing yourself small pain; he adds that knowing better does not stop you.

questions.prompt: What distinction does the writer draw at the end about the third book?
answer: being written is different from being planned
it is being written rather than planned
the difference between written and planned
being written is not being planned
questions.explanation: He says it is being written, 'which is a different thing from being planned'.

questions.prompt: Which word best describes the writer's tone throughout?
questions.explanation: His answers are dry, honest about his own weaknesses, and lightly humorous rather than proud or bitter.

tests.title: A committee meeting
tests.description: A meeting in which decisions are made and reported. Competency levels 3.6 and 6.11: reports information, and reported speech.
tests.instructions: Listen to the meeting and follow what is decided. Answer the questions, then submit.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Listen to part of a school welfare committee meeting.

script.speaker: Chair
script.text: Item three: the condition of the science laboratory. Mr Fernando, you inspected it.

script.speaker: Mr Fernando
script.text: I did. Four of the twelve gas taps are leaking, and the emergency shower has not worked since last year.

script.speaker: Chair
script.text: Has this been reported before?

script.speaker: Mr Fernando
script.text: Twice. I was told in March that the parts had been ordered. When I asked again in July, I was told the same thing.

script.speaker: Mrs Silva
script.text: Then perhaps we should stop asking and start writing. A letter from this committee carries more weight than a conversation in a corridor.

script.speaker: Chair
script.text: Agreed. Mrs Silva, would you draft it? Mr Fernando, please photograph the taps and attach the photographs.

script.speaker: Mrs Silva
script.text: I shall have it ready by Monday. I would suggest we also copy it to the zonal office.

script.speaker: Chair
script.text: Noted. And until the shower is repaired, practical work involving acids is suspended. Is that accepted?

script.speaker: Mr Fernando
script.text: Accepted.

questions.prompt: Complete the minutes.
questions.explanation: Four taps leak; Mrs Silva will draft the letter and have it ready by Monday.

questions.prompt: How long has the emergency shower been broken?
questions.explanation: Mr Fernando says it has not worked since last year.

questions.prompt: What was Mr Fernando told when he asked in July?
options: The same thing he was told in March
questions.explanation: He says, 'When I asked again in July, I was told the same thing.'

questions.prompt: Why does Mrs Silva suggest writing rather than asking?
options: Because nobody is available to ask
Because a committee letter carries more weight
Because it is a school rule
questions.explanation: She says a letter from the committee carries more weight than a conversation in a corridor.

questions.prompt: What is Mr Fernando asked to do?
answer: photograph the taps and attach the photographs
questions.explanation: The chair asks him to photograph the taps and attach the photographs to the letter.

questions.prompt: What is suspended until the shower is repaired?
questions.explanation: The chair suspends practical work involving acids until the shower is repaired.

tests.title: Advice before the examination
tests.description: A teacher gives structured advice, signalled by discourse markers. Competency levels 3.7 and 3.8: recognizes discourse markers and takes notes from an oral presentation.
tests.instructions: Listen to the advice and note the main points. Answer the questions, then submit.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Listen to a teacher speaking to a class before the Ordinary Level examination.

script.speaker: Teacher
script.text: You have six weeks. I want to say four things, and none of them is about working harder.

script.speaker: Teacher
script.text: First, work in shorter periods. Forty minutes of full attention is worth more than three hours of turning pages while thinking about something else.

script.speaker: Teacher
script.text: Secondly, write. You cannot revise writing by reading. If the paper asks you to write a letter, you must have written letters, not read about them.

script.speaker: Teacher
script.text: Thirdly, and this is the one you will ignore: sleep. A tired candidate misreads the question. Almost every serious mistake I have marked began with misreading.

script.speaker: Teacher
script.text: Finally, in the hall itself, read the whole paper before you write a single word. Two minutes spent reading will save you twenty.

script.speaker: Teacher
script.text: In short: shorter sessions, actual writing, proper sleep, and read before you answer. That is all I have.

questions.prompt: Put the teacher's four pieces of advice in the order given.
items: Read the whole paper before writing
questions.explanation: The markers First, Secondly, Thirdly and Finally set out the four in this order.

questions.prompt: What does the teacher say at the start about his advice?
options: None of it is about working harder
It is only for weak students
It applies to one subject only
questions.explanation: He says, 'I want to say four things, and none of them is about working harder.'

questions.prompt: Complete the notes.

lines.label: Length of a good study session:

questions.explanation: Six weeks remain; forty minutes of full attention; two minutes reading the paper saves twenty.

questions.prompt: Why does the teacher say you cannot revise writing by reading?
options: Writing is a skill that must be practised, not studied
questions.explanation: He says if the paper asks you to write a letter, you must have written letters, not read about them.

questions.prompt: Which piece of advice does the teacher predict students will ignore?
questions.explanation: He introduces it with 'and this is the one you will ignore: sleep.'

questions.prompt: According to the teacher, how does almost every serious mistake begin?
questions.explanation: He says almost every serious mistake he has marked began with misreading.
